utility.notes: East Palo Alto is a well-documented San Mateo County city, and San Mateo County is uniformly PG&E territory, consistent with PG&E service already established for other San Mateo County records this session. (Note: East Palo Alto is a distinct city from Palo Alto, which has its own municipal utility, CPAU, across the county line in Santa Clara County.)

value.name: WestLight Energy (formerly Peninsula Clean Energy) - ECOplus (default)
value.notes: East Palo Alto's own community resources page references Peninsula Clean Energy (now WestLight Energy) community outreach events, and WestLight Energy's own community-programs pages name East Palo Alto within its San Mateo County service area. San Mateo County's CCA program enrolls all county jurisdictions' customers by default (opt-out model), consistent with the default-enrollment pattern directly confirmed for other San Mateo County cities (e.g. South San Francisco, Menlo Park) this session, though East Palo Alto's own page did not itself explicitly state 'default enrollment' in the content reviewed.

permit_authority.value: City of East Palo Alto Building Services Division

interconnection_url.notes: PG&E's own Net Energy Metering (NEM) program page — a utility-wide fact already established for other PG&E-territory records in this dataset.

value.name: SGIP - Residential Solar and Storage Equity
value.administrator: Pacific Gas and Electric Company (PG&E), under the CPUC's Self-Generation Incentive Program
value.description: Storage incentive of $1,100/kWh paired with a solar incentive of $3,100/kW, funded via a $280 million CPUC-authorized budget that opened for reservations June 2, 2025. Administered by PG&E across its entire distribution territory, which includes East Palo Alto/San Mateo County.
value.eligibility: PG&E or SCE residential customers (general market tier)

battery_programs.notes: Same statewide CPUC-administered SGIP program already confirmed for other PG&E-territory records this session, reused as a utility-level fact.

value.notes: Staff contact applicants within two business days regarding next steps, per the city's own Building Services page. This is a response-time commitment, not necessarily the full permit-issuance timeline.
